newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore gas oil, jet firm, fuel oil steady.
newsitem.headline: Singapore gas oil, jet firm, fuel oil steady.

text.p: Singapore oil products were mixed on Tuesday with gas oil rising on the back of overnight rally in London gas oil futures, while fuel oil and light distillates were steady, traders said on Tuesday.
Traders said the colder weather in the west would make it more difficult to move gas oil barrels to eastwards.

They said a Japanese trader sold 240,000 barrels of gas oil to a MidEast trader at $32.95 a barrel for Jan 1-5 lifting fob. The same buyer was also seeking to buy an offer from a Singapore trader for Jan 8-12 lifting at $32.50. This was higher than offers seen on Monday around $32.20.

Gas oil swaps also rebounded to trade as high as $32.20, up from Monday's $31.70. Taiwan's CPC has awarded a second gas oil term contract to Singapore trader Hin Leong trading at 45-50 a barrel over Singapore spot quotes, fob. Traders said with the recovery seen on gas oil, premiums have also risen with a bid seen at 55 cents, but traders said levels should be higher than that.

Jet fuel was offered by a European major at $33.30 for early January and saw a bid from a US trader. Traders said jet fuel sentiment remained strong with Japanese buyers still keen to seek early January barrels of dual purpose kerosene.

Taiwan bought only two 250,000-barrel cargoes of 95-octane reformate for January 18-27 delivery at $26 a barrel c+f Taiwan, and February 11-20 at $25.50, from a western trader and a European major. Sources said prices were below the last tender for January, awarded at $26.80 but remained aggressive. January swaps were quoted at $25.00/$25.65, steady with Monday's $25.60 offer. Naphtha January swaps were traded twice at $24 a barrel with a Dutch trader buying from a Japanese and a Chinese trader. Levels were unchanged from Monday's offer at $23.90. Tokyo's open-spec firmed but Singapore levels were steady as freight costs to Japan remained high.--Singapore Newsroom (65-870 3084)
